sourcedFrom: Ruger LC9s & EC9s Lightweight Compact Pistols Instruction Manual — PM1188 (cover part code not printed; see MANIFEST) (2024)
cleanIntro: One manual covers the LC9s and EC9s. The step that catches people is the magazine disconnect — an inert magazine goes in before the pistol will come apart.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction, press the magazine latch and remove the magazine.
steps.quote: Keep pistol pointed in a safe direction. Press the magazine latch and remove the magazine
steps.cite: Ruger LC9s & EC9s Lightweight Compact Pistols Instruction Manual — PM1188 (cover part code not printed; see MANIFEST) — Disassembly, step 1, p.21
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Safety to fire, lock the slide open
steps.action: With the safety in the "fire" position, pull the slide to the rear and lock it open by pushing upward on the slide stop.
steps.prose: Safety to FIRE — counter-intuitive, but the slide will not lock back otherwise.
steps.quote: With the safety in the "fire" position, pull the slide to the rear and lock the slide in the open position by pushing upward on the slide stop
steps.cite: Ruger LC9s & EC9s Lightweight Compact Pistols Instruction Manual — PM1188 (cover part code not printed; see MANIFEST) — Disassembly, step 2, p.21

steps.title: Verify the chamber
steps.action: Inspect the chamber and verify that it is empty.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and verify that it is empty
steps.cite: Ruger LC9s & EC9s Lightweight Compact Pistols Instruction Manual — PM1188 (cover part code not printed; see MANIFEST) — Disassembly, step 3, p.21

steps.title: The magazine disconnect — this is the step people miss
steps.action: With the pistol pointed in a safe direction, insert the orange inert magazine (or an empty one). This pistol has a magazine disconnect, and the inert magazine is how you safely release striker tension before disassembly.
steps.prose: Ruger supplies the orange magazine for exactly this. Without a magazine in the well the striker cannot be let down and the pistol will not strip.
steps.quote: The orange inert magazine is provided as a means to allow you to safely release tension on the striker prior to disassembly.
steps.cite: Ruger LC9s & EC9s Lightweight Compact Pistols Instruction Manual — PM1188 (cover part code not printed; see MANIFEST) — Disassembly, step 5, p.22

steps.title: Takedown plate down, pin out
steps.action: Using a finger or a soft tool, push the takedown plate down to expose the takedown pin, then remove the pin.
steps.prose: Soft tool — a screwdriver blade marks the plate and the frame behind it.
steps.quote: Using a finger or a "soft" tool, push the takedown plate down
steps.cite: Ruger LC9s & EC9s Lightweight Compact Pistols Instruction Manual — PM1188 (cover part code not printed; see MANIFEST) — Disassembly, step 6, p.22

deepAbsentReason: The LC9s/EC9s manual documents the field strip only. No disassembly past it is published, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent patch through the bore, correctly sized brush, then dry patches until clean
Wipe the feed ramp and chamber mouth

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Scrub the breech face and around the extractor
Wipe the striker channel DRY — no oil in an ignition channel
One drop of oil on each slide rail

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wipe magazine bodies dry, inside and out — no oil where ammunition sits

reassembly: Be certain the chamber and magazine are empty.
With the slide held upside down, reinstall the barrel and push it rearward into its locked position.
Be sure the guide rod spring is centred on the guide rod head, then seat the guide rod assembly with its rear end against the barrel lug.
With the firearm held upside down, reinstall the slide onto the frame and close it as if the pistol were fully assembled.
fncheck: With the magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, check the safety and the magazine disconnect behave as the manual describes, pointed in a safe direction.
